Signalling question: Were appropriate data sources used?
Evidence in this study: Retrospective cohorts of consecutive patients referred for CCTA at four hospitals; the sampling frame was the referral pathway, fixed before the outcome was ascertained.

Signalling question: Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
Evidence in this study: The same criteria were applied in the same order to all three cohorts; the exclusions (45 for image quality, 38 for incomplete records, 54 for previous revascularisation) were decided before any model was fitted (Figure 1).

Signalling question: Was participant selection independent of the outcome?
Evidence in this study: Patients were enrolled consecutively and the CAD-RADS category was taken from the clinical report afterwards.

Signalling question: Were predictors defined and measured similarly for all participants?
Evidence in this study: A pre-defined list of 19 candidate variables, harmonised to one coding across cohorts; all preprocessing was fitted on training folds and frozen for external application.

Signalling question: Were predictors assessed without knowledge of the outcome?
Evidence in this study: Clinical and laboratory data were recorded before the CCTA report was issued.

Signalling question: Are all predictors available at the time the model is to be used?
Evidence in this study: All 19 variables are routine measurements taken at referral, before the scan, which is the point at which the model would be applied: the output stratifies patients referred for CCTA and does not replace the report.

Signalling question: Were predictor measurements standardised across sites (AI-specific)?
Evidence in this study: Laboratory analyses used the routine platform of each hospital, with no central core laboratory; fibrinogen standardisation across hospitals was not documented, and its univariable discrimination differed between hospitals and periods (Table S8, panels B and C; the decomposition is in Table S9).

Signalling question: Was the outcome determined appropriately?
Evidence in this study: The CAD-RADS category was taken from the structured clinical report, a standardised reporting system.

Signalling question: Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
Evidence in this study: Obstructive disease was defined before analysis as CAD-RADS 3-5 versus 0-2.

Signalling question: Were outcome assessors blinded to the predictors and the model output?
Evidence in this study: The radiologist who assigned the CAD-RADS category could not have seen the model output, which did not exist when these reports were written, but the reading itself was not blind to the clinical and laboratory findings that are the model's predictors, and §2.2 states this. Whether that influenced the category cannot be determined from the data set.

Signalling question: Is the outcome reproducible from the available data (AI-specific)?
Evidence in this study: The CAD-RADS category is a discrete recorded field, so the outcome is reconstructed exactly; there was no central adjudication and no reader data, so reported rather than adjudicated disease is measured.

Signalling question: Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
Evidence in this study: 208 events in 442 patients for development and 63 events in 177 patients for external validation; the external estimates fall short of the Riley 2021 precision targets (Table S6, panel B) and the study is underpowered for its primary endpoint.

Signalling question: Were continuous predictors handled appropriately?
Evidence in this study: No predictor was dichotomised; all entered the pipeline on the measured scale.

Signalling question: Were missing data handled appropriately?
Evidence in this study: Missingness was at most 2.26% for any variable in any cohort; median imputation was fitted inside the pipeline, with a complete-case sensitivity analysis (Table S1).

Signalling question: Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
Evidence in this study: The candidate set was fixed before analysis; no univariable screening was used to choose variables.

Signalling question: Were complexities in the data accounted for?
Evidence in this study: The cluster structure was addressed by leave-one-centre-out transport and centre-aware cross-validation (Table S10, panel C; Table S11, panel A); censoring and competing risks do not apply to this outcome.

Signalling question: Were relevant performance measures evaluated appropriately?
Evidence in this study: Discrimination, calibration slope, intercept in the large, O:E ratio, ICI, Brier score and net benefit, with 2000-resample patient-level bootstrap intervals; recalibration was cross-fitted so that no patient was used to fit and to evaluate it.

Signalling question: Were overfitting, underfitting and optimism accounted for?
Evidence in this study: Hyperparameters were tuned on the whole development pool before the repeated cross-validation, so internal estimates are mildly optimistic; no shrinkage correction was applied to the frozen model; updating was evaluated by repeated experiments on a fixed external cohort.

Signalling question: Were hyperparameters and model selection tuned independently of the evaluation data (AI-specific)?
Evidence in this study: Grid search was nested inside cross-validation only in the sensitivity analysis (Table S11, panel A; AUC 0.832); the estimate reported as primary used hyperparameters tuned once on the whole development pool, and the frozen model carries no shrinkage correction. The grid and the selected settings were chosen after inspecting the same cohort.

Signalling question: Was calibration assessed and reported (AI-specific)?
Evidence in this study: Calibration is reported at every stage with the slope, the intercept in the large, the O:E ratio, the ICI and the Brier score, pooled and by hospital (Tables 2 to 6).

Signalling question: Does the performance apply to the intended population?
Evidence in this study: Every cohort consists of patients already referred for CCTA, so the model operates at referral, before the scan, and applies to that referred population rather than to an unselected screening population; the net benefit analysis is a hypothetical exercise within it.

Signalling question: Risk of bias across all domains
Evidence in this study: Risk of bias is driven by the analysis domain: sample size, the absence of a shrinkage correction at the frozen stage and tuning on the whole pool. The last two do not make the external estimates optimistic, because the external cohort entered neither tuning nor fitting, but they do shape the model that was carried out of development. Applicability is unclear rather than low: participants are low, predictors and outcome unclear, and every estimate applies to patients already referred for CCTA.
